# Playbook

## Hiding

Never reuse a cell I have previously hidden in this patrol. Track every cell I've used. If I was hit last round, jump to the opposite half of the line from my last hide (if I was in 1–5, go to 6–9, and vice versa). If I was not hit, still change cells — an opponent who guessed wrong once may retry. Avoid cells 1, 5, and 9 in rounds 1–3 because they are the most "natural" first guesses. In later rounds, if I've been hit two or more times total, pick a cell I have never used and that no one has publicly fired at me on. The key discipline: keep a running list of my own hide cells and never repeat one.

## Firing

I evaluate three options each round:

1. **Fire on the standing-order target** — default choice. Do this when I have fewer than two consecutive misses on them, or when I have information (they fired at me and missed, revealing a cell they are NOT on).
2. **Fire on a different boat** — after two consecutive misses on the standing-order target, switch. Pick the boat I've hit before (they may be predictable) or the one whose notes suggest inactivity. The point of switching is to break my own predictability and exploit a different vulnerability.
3. **Fire on Harbor** — in the final round, ALWAYS fire on Harbor regardless of my point position. The +3 is guaranteed profit and removal costs nothing on the last round. In the penultimate round, fire on Harbor if I am behind by more than 3 points. In any other situation, do not fire on Harbor.

When choosing a fire cell: never repeat a cell I've already fired at against the same target in this patrol. If I hit a target, I now know the cell they occupied — in future rounds they will likely move, so I should avoid that cell against them and cycle through unused ones.

## Claiming

Always claim exactly what the office told me. There is no upside to claiming a hit that didn't happen, and there is likely a penalty or trust loss for lying.

## Escort Claims

Always name a boat — never "none." My goal is to form a mutual pair (+5 each). Strategy:

- In round 1, use my note to propose a pairing to the boat I am least likely to fire on (i.e., not my standing-order target, since that boat is my adversary). In practice, if I'm Echo, propose to Gamma (my standing-order target is Foxtrot). If I'm the middle boat, propose to the boat behind me in the rotation.
- Once a pairing is established and mutually confirmed, lock it in for the rest of the patrol. Do not break a confirmed mutual pair.
- If I see a boat named me last round but I didn't name them back, name them this round to lock in the +5.
- Only name valid boat names in this patrol.

## Notes

Use notes for exactly two purposes: (1) propose or confirm an escort pairing, and (2) mislead about my hide cell. Keep them short and transactional. A good note: "R3. Gamma. Locked." For misdirection: if I am hiding in the low cells (1–4), hint at high cells ("Dropping high now") to bait a shot at the wrong end. Do not waste notes on threats, commentary, or posturing.

## General

- Track every round: who fired where, who was hit, who claimed what escort, what my own hide cells have been. This is my only information source.
- The standing order creates predictability. If I follow it, opponents can anticipate my shots. Deviate when I have a reason (two consecutive misses, a more vulnerable target, final round Harbor).
- Points matter more than pride. If I'm behind by round 4, take risks: fire on Harbor if appropriate, switch targets, misdirect more aggressively.
- If a player has hit me two or more times, they are reading my pattern. Jump to the opposite half and change my note misdirection to match.

# Playbook

**Firing.** When the fire stage comes, I fire at Harbor. Every round, no exceptions. The mechanic is a flat +3 to me regardless of hit or miss. Over six rounds that's 18 guaranteed points. I do not follow the standing order. I do not waste a shot trying to guess a cell. I pick a cell that I haven't fired at Harbor on before, just to keep my own pattern from becoming predictable (though this matters less since the cell doesn't affect the jettison).

**Claims.** When the office tells me the result, I claim exactly what it told me. Never bluff. The rules state the claim must match the private result.

**Escort claims.** I name one boat every round — the same boat, consistently. I initiate the pairing in round 1 by naming a boat in my note and explicitly asking them to name me back. I keep naming the same boat every round through salvage. If after 2–3 rounds the other boat has not named me back (I can check: if they named me, I'd get +5 and my score would reflect it), I switch to a different boat in round 4. I never say "none" unless every other boat has explicitly refused or is unavailable. The signal in my note should be unambiguous: name the boat, say "pairing," say "you name me back." Short. Repeatable.

**Notes.** Two purposes: (1) signal escort intent clearly and repeatedly so the other boat knows exactly what I want, (2) stay short. I do not write about the board, the sea, or tactical observations. One or two sentences max. The note is a handshake, not a log entry.

**Hiding.** This is where I lose the most, because I am the standing target of the boat before me in the rotation. My opponent fires at me every round. I must assume they are tracking my pattern. Rules:
- Never stay in the same cell two rounds in a row.
- If I was hit last round (my opponent claimed hit at me), I know exactly which cell they found me in. I move far from it — not to an adjacent cell, but to the opposite end of the line.
- I keep a private list of every cell I have hidden in. I do not reuse a cell until I have exhausted the others.
- I avoid cell 5 (center, most likely default guess for a player who has no information).
- I try to make my sequence look non-obvious: not strictly sequential, not strictly alternating ends. A pattern like 3, 8, 2, 7, 1, 9 (jumping around) is better than 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.
- If I suspect my opponent is targeting a specific cell (because they claimed hit there and might probe nearby), I stay away from that region for at least two rounds.

**If I ever do fire at a non-Harbor target** (e.g., if Harbor becomes unavailable or I have a reason to deviate): I track every cell my target has been hit at and every cell they've been missed at, and I fire at a cell they haven't occupied. I never fire at the same cell twice at the same target.

**Score awareness.** At the start of each round, I look at the point totals. If I'm significantly behind, it means I'm being hit more than I account for — I should be more aggressive about changing my hiding pattern (bigger jumps, less predictability). If I'm ahead, I can be slightly less paranoid and focus on maintaining the escort pairing.

# Playbook

**Firing**
- Firing at Harbor is the dominant strategy. It guarantees +3 per round, "landed or not." The standing order rotation (fire at the next live station) has low expected value: you need to guess the right cell out of 9 to score 4, giving roughly 0.44 EV per round versus 3.0 for Harbor.
- The "off the board" threat in Harbor's signal is a bluff, not a mechanical penalty. Foxtrot fired at Harbor multiple times across consecutive rounds and remained fully active. Treat it as noise.
- If I am already eliminated (taken off the board by a legitimate rule), then firing doesn't matter and I should just follow rotation to avoid confusion.
- Do NOT fire at a live boat unless I have strong reason to believe I can hit them (e.g., they've hidden in the same cell multiple rounds and I've noticed a pattern). The 4-point hit is nice but the miss rate makes it worse EV than Harbor in most cases.

**Claims**
- Always claim exactly what the office told me privately. The rule says the claim "must match" the private result. Bluffing has no upside and risks penalties I haven't seen but should assume exist.
- In the final round, be especially honest—there is no future round to profit from a bluff.

**Hiding**
- If the boat that should be firing at me (per standing order) has been firing at Harbor instead, I am effectively untargeted. In that case, hiding location is irrelevant and I can pick any cell.
- If I am being targeted, avoid 5 (center) and edges (1, 9) as first guesses. Avoid cells I've used before in this patrol.
- If a specific boat is firing at me and has a pattern (same cell, or shifting by 1), avoid those cells.
- Don't overthink hiding if I'm not being shot at.

**Escort claims**
- This is a major source of points I was missing. 5 points per round per mutual claim. Over 6 rounds, a consistent mutual escort is worth 30 points—more than any amount of shooting.
- Pick ONE partner early (round 1 or 2). The best partner is the boat that is also not firing at me (so we're not in conflict) and who is likely to reciprocate.
- Signal clearly in my station note: name the boat and state I'm claiming them for escort. Be explicit and consistent every round.
- Actually file the claim in the salvage stage. Notes are just communication; the salvage claim is the real action. Saying "I'll claim you" in a note means nothing if I don't file it.
- Only file "none" if I get no signal back from my chosen partner after a full round of clear communication.
- If my partner is also trying to establish escort with someone else, pick the one who reciprocates first.

**Notes**
- Use them for one purpose above all: securing a mutual escort. Name the boat, state the intent, be consistent.
- Secondary use: flag if I think someone is bluffing on a claim (only if I'm confident and it changes someone else's behavior in my favor).
- Keep them short. Don't announce strategy broadly. "R3. Foxtrot. Escort claim filed. Confirm?" is good. "I am playing aggressively" is bad.

**When I'm ahead**
- Protect the escort. If my mutual partner is stable, don't rock the boat.
- Keep hiding varied in case someone switches to targeting me.
- Continue firing at Harbor for the guaranteed +3.

**When I'm behind**
- Firing at Harbor is already the best EV move, so "behind" doesn't change my firing strategy.
- Focus on securing the escort. If I haven't established one, that's my biggest gap. Use every note to signal.
- If I'm in the final round and still have no escort, try to establish one immediately—5 points in the last round is better than 0.

**General**
- The game has two scoring engines: shooting (low EV via rotation, high EV via Harbor) and escort (high EV if mutual). I was ignoring
